Notes: Multi-tag Host column ('vertebrates,human' etc.) -- human is the one mutually-exclusive priority tag (wins over vertebrate whenever both are present). Verified against all 61,684 raw records: this count = every record whose Host field contains 'human', regardless of what else co-occurs.

DeepHoF's residual microbial class. The study never defines the word but states that its five host types 'covered all the living organism hosts', which leaves germ as the microbial remainder, and its records confirm it: read by viral taxon, 11,529 of the 12,020 are viruses of bacteria or archaea and 491 of fungi, protists and algae (evidence: scripts/resolve_germ.py). Excluded as non-eukaryotic, on the same ground as RNAVirHost's `Bacteria` and Host Taxon Predictor's `Prokaryote/Archaea`. This drops the 491 fungal and protist records with it, because the released tag does not separate them. Still NOT mutually exclusive with DeepHoF's other four categories -- see Potential_double_count.
Overlaps_with: Humans, Non-human vertebrates, Invertebrates, Plants -- counted independently, a record can appear here AND elsewhere

Infects a vertebrate host as well as its mosquito vector. The released class names the host range, not the host taxon, so the vertebrate side is unresolved; the vector side is Culicidae and is not counted again here, since the label is one record and the review counts a record once.
Replicates only in mosquito cells, so the mosquito is the host rather than a vector. Routed to Culicidae, the family the review already uses for mosquito labels from other tools.
